record.paper_title: Doubly-Special Relativity: First Results and Key Open Problems
record.original_question: Can a Doubly-Special Relativity theory explain the apparent Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin (GZK) cosmic-ray anomaly by producing a sufficiently large modification of the threshold for pion production of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays on cosmic microwave background photons? The paper notes that DSR generically changes thresholds, but specifically states that the known DSR1 and DSR2 constructions shift the GZK limit only very slightly. The unresolved problem is whether some other DSR theory can produce a significant change in the GZK limit while remaining compatible with the relativity principle.

evidence.quote: 7.4. Can DSR solve the GZK anomaly?

While DSR theories do generically predict anomalous thresholds (and therefore generically predict a different value of the GZK limit), as mentioned in DSR1 and DSR2 the change in the value of the GZK limit is very small, and could not be used to explain away the paradoxical ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observations.
Even looking beyond DSR1 and DSR2 it appears hard to find a DSR theory which would significantly affect the GZK limit.

artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent analyses indicate that standard Doubly-Special Relativity does not produce a significant modification of the GZK threshold, and cosmic-ray observations (HiRes, Auger) have largely confirmed a GZK-like cutoff, diminishing the original motivation. However, no definitive proof exists that no DSR theory consistent with the relativity principle could produce a large GZK shift, so the precise question remains formally unresolved.

status_evidence.snippet: Standard doubly special relativity does not predict any suppression of the GZK cutoff, contrary to models with a preferred frame.
status_evidence.claim: Standard DSR does not modify the GZK threshold significantly.

status_evidence.title: AUGER-HiRes results and models of Lorentz symmetry violation
status_evidence.snippet: Auger and HiRes observations of a GZK-like cutoff constrain Lorentz-violating modifications of UHECR thresholds.
status_evidence.claim: Observational data is consistent with the standard GZK cutoff, reducing the phenomenological motivation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In special relativity, the energy–momentum dispersion relation E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4 together with energy–momentum conservation fixes a kinematic threshold for the photopion production reaction p + γ → p + π, in which an ultra-high-energy proton scatters off a cosmic microwave background photon. This threshold gives rise to the Greisen–Zatsepin–Kuzmin (GZK) bound on the energy of cosmic-ray protons that can reach Earth from cosmologically distant sources.

A Doubly-Special Relativity (DSR) theory is a deformation of special-relativistic kinematics characterized by two invariant scales: the speed of light c and an additional invariant momentum/energy scale κ (typically identified with the Planck scale). It is defined by:
(i) a one-parameter family of nonlinear realizations of the Lorentz group on momentum space that leaves both c and κ invariant for every inertial observer (the relativity principle), and
(ii) a modified dispersion relation F(E, p; κ) = m^2 and a (generally nonlinear) composition law (E_1, p_1) ⊕ (E_2, p_2) for momenta of multi-particle states, compatible with (i).

Two explicit constructions, here labelled DSR1 and DSR2, are known; for both, an analysis of the reaction p + γ → p + π using the deformed dispersion relation and the deformed conservation law yields a GZK threshold that differs from the special-relativistic value by an amount too small to account for any apparent deficit of the GZK suppression in ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray data.

Problem. Does there exist a Doubly-Special Relativity theory — that is, a deformed kinematics satisfying the relativity principle with invariants c and κ — whose modified dispersion relation and modified energy–momentum conservation law produce a quantitatively significant shift of the threshold of the photopion reaction p + γ → p + π on cosmic microwave background photons, of a magnitude sufficient to explain a substantial violation or relaxation of the standard GZK bound on ultra-high-energy cosmic rays? Either exhibit such a DSR theory explicitly, or prove that within the class of DSR theories compatible with the relativity principle no such significant modification of the GZK threshold is possible.
